title: The EASM (ZEASM) API: organization scoping, clients, paging and the Postman collection

prose.text: Paths and methods are generated: run `node scripts/kb.mjs surface easm`, and read field descriptions and enums in `vendor/zscaler-api-specs/automate-zscaler/openapi/easm.openapi.json`. This subject holds how calls are scoped and paged and where the clients fall short.

prose.label: What it is.
prose.text: {{name}} The OneAPI base path is in [[shared.oneapi.base-urls:base-path-table]], and the guide's example that drops the `/easm` prefix in [[shared.oneapi.base-urls:easm-example-path]].

prose.label: Organization first.
prose.text: {{org-scoping}} {{org-model}} Whether tenants normally have several organizations is open {{gap:multi-org}}.

prose.label: Resources.
prose.text: Findings are in [[easm.findings]] and lookalike domains in [[easm.lookalike-domains]].

checks.do: Which organization ID the call uses: list organizations first and take the id.
For an asset inventory, whether a raw API call is needed, since no SDK or MCP client lists assets.
When copying a Postman EASM request, whether its raw URL is one of the three malformed ones.

name.statement: The API is the External Attack Surface Management API; the Python SDK calls the product ZEASM and serves it at `/easm/easm-ui/v1`.

sdk-resources.statement: The SDK's `ZEASMService` exposes three resources, `organizations`, `findings` and `lookalike_domains`, added in release 1.9.6.

quotes: Added External Attach Surface Management(EASM) Endpoints

assets-api-only.statement: The asset endpoints (list assets, and an asset's certificates, services and technologies) are in the API contract but no SDK resource or MCP tool calls them.
assets-api-only.conditions: Rests on the generated surface for easm: the four /assets paths map to no Python method, and the MCP EASM toolsets list only organization, finding and lookalike tools.

python-only.statement: No Go SDK package, Terraform resource or Ansible module covers EASM; the Python SDK and the MCP server are its only clients.
python-only.conditions: Rests on the generated surface for easm, which lists Python modules and no Go packages or Terraform resources, and on a grep of the Go SDK's zscaler/ tree (packages zcc, zdx, zia, ziam, zpa, ztw, zwa) and of the ZIA and ZPA Ansible plugins at their pins for easm and zeasm found nothing.

org-scoping.statement: Organizations are listed with no arguments; the finding and lookalike methods take the organization ID first and build URLs under `/organizations/{org_id}`, using the `id` of an organization from that list.

org-model.statement: An organization carries only `id` and `name` (both strings); the organizations response also has `next_page`, `prev_page` and `total_results`.

expect.description: The unique identifier of an organization

id.description: The unique identifier of an organization

list-paging.statement: Finding and lookalike list responses carry a results list and a total count (`results`, `total_results`) and no page fields, while the assets list returns `next_link` and `prev_link` URLs carrying a page offset.

expect.description: The total number of findings in the response
The list of findings detected for an organization
The total number of lookalike domains present in the response
The list of lookalike domains identified for the seed domains configured for an organization
The URL with a page offset to access the subsequent set of assets
The URL with a page offset to access the previous set of assets

sdk-no-list-args.statement: The SDK's findings and lookalike-domains list methods take only the organization ID: their signatures have no paging, sorting or filter arguments.

client-search.statement: SDK responses support client-side filtering and projection with `resp.search(expression)` in JMESPath syntax.

quotes: The response object supports client-side filtering and projection via ``resp.search(expression)``.

postman-asset-params.statement: The OneAPI Postman collection documents list-assets query parameters: `limit` (default 100, max 1000), `offset`, `sort`, `search`, `riskLevel`, `status`, `country`, `state`, `type`, `lastSeen`, `firstSeen` and `certificateExpiration`.

quotes: "description": "Number of assets to return per page (default 100, max 1000)"
"description": "Filter by certificate expiration date (used when type is 'CERTIFICATE')."

postman-lookalike-params.statement: The Postman list-lookalike-domains request carries `limit`, `offset`, `sort`, `search`, `status`, `riskLevel`, `riskCategory` and `deceptionMethods` query parameters.

postman-url-defects.statement: Three Postman EASM requests have malformed raw URLs: list assets appends an extra `}}` to `{{EASMBaseUrl}}`, get lookalike-domain details an extra `}`, and list lookalike domains omits the slash before `organizations`.

list-query-params.summary: The API contract lists no query parameters for the asset and lookalike lists; the Postman collection documents paging and filters for both.

positions.says: List assets takes only the Authorization header and the orgId path parameter.
List assets takes limit, offset, sort, search and filter query parameters.

quotes: "description": "Number of assets to return per page (default 100, max 1000)"

list-query-params.impact: Large inventories may need limit and offset, which only Postman documents and no SDK method sends; test them against a tenant before relying on them.

multi-org.title: How tenants use more than one EASM organization
multi-org.detail: Unverified legacy statement: normal multi-org tenancy is not established. The organizations response is a list with paging fields and the SDK and MCP return a list, but no source says when a tenant has more than one organization (for example per business unit).
multi-org.blocks: answering which organization's findings a question is about
